adaptationNotes: Source item is an H5P fill-in-the-blank dialogue; reformatted into heading/text/example blocks with the conversation reconstructed from the exercise's accepted answers.
Fill-in-the-blank interaction converted to one multiple-choice question with the same learning goal (choosing a reply to 'How are you?').
Vietnamese translations on example blocks added by SE (not present in the source).

Two third-party items are included as click-to-load external embeds from their original hosts — one English with Jennifer YouTube video (AzES-nhQFzk) and the original PCC memory-game activity (H5P id 18); nothing was copied or rehosted.
Remaining chapter items (dialog cards, extra dialogue, second video) left un-embedded to keep this to one focused lesson; reachable via the source link.
source.attribution: Adapted from 'Level 01 Module 01 Greetings 01' by Tim Krause, A Digital Workbook for Beginning ESOL (Portland Community College / Open Oregon Educational Resources), CC0 1.0. Adapted by Simple English.

blocks.text: In English, we greet people with short phrases like “Hello” or “Hi”.
After the greeting, people often ask “How are you?”. A friendly answer is “Fine, thank you.”

— How are you?
— Fine, thank you. How are you?
— Good. Thank you.
blocks.translation:
— Bạn có khỏe không?
— Tôi khỏe, cảm ơn. Còn bạn?
— Tôi ổn. Cảm ơn bạn.
